overview: South Korea is a country in East Asia, on the southern half of the Korean Peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Seoul. Korea was divided after the Second World War, and the Korean War of 1950–53 ended with a ceasefire but no peace treaty. South Korea grew rapidly into one of the world's leading economies and is known for its technology, cars, films and K-pop.

geography.text: About 70 percent of South Korea is mountainous, with the Taebaek Mountains running down the east. Most people live on the plains and in the river valleys of the west. It has coasts on the Yellow Sea, the Korea Strait and the Sea of Japan, and thousands of islands, the largest being Jeju, a volcanic island with the country's highest peak, Hallasan.

history.text: Korea was united for centuries under kingdoms such as Silla, Goryeo and Joseon; under King Sejong in the 1440s the Korean alphabet, Hangul, was created. Japan ruled Korea from 1910 to 1945. After the Korean War of 1950–53, South Korea grew from one of the poorest countries in the world into a wealthy democracy.

events.title: Hangul
events.text: King Sejong creates the Korean alphabet.

events.title: Korean War
events.text: North Korea invades; UN forces led by the US defend the South.

events.title: Democracy
events.text: Mass protests lead to free presidential elections.

government.text: South Korea is a presidential republic. The President is elected for a single five-year term and leads the government. The National Assembly has one chamber. In December 2024 President Yoon Suk Yeol briefly declared martial law; he was impeached and removed from office in 2025, and a new President was elected.

economy.text: South Korea grew from one of the poorest countries in the world in the 1950s into one of the richest. It is a world leader in computer chips, phones, ships, cars and batteries, through companies such as Samsung, Hyundai and LG.

culture.text: Korean pop culture, the 'Korean Wave', has spread worldwide through K-pop bands such as BTS and BLACKPINK, films such as Parasite and series such as Squid Game. Kimchi, spicy fermented cabbage, is eaten with almost every meal. The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was invented in the 1440s.

items.title: K-pop
items.text: Korean pop music with fans across the world.

items.title: Parasite
items.text: The first non-English film to win the Oscar for Best Picture, in 2020.

items.title: Kimjang
items.text: Making kimchi together for winter, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Baseball and football are the most popular sports. South Korea hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics and the 2018 Winter Olympics, and co-hosted the 2002 World Cup, where it reached the semi-finals. It dominates archery and taekwondo, which began in Korea.

items.title: Archery
items.text: South Korean women have won every Olympic team archery gold since 1988.
